Four inventory services import `src/domain/state-machines.ts` and call its transition rules directly.

| Service | Machine used | Call site |
|---|---|---|
| `src/inventory/inventory.service.ts` | `InventoryUnitStateMachine` | line 466, a generic unit status change to `targetStatus` |
| `src/inventory/reservation.service.ts` | `ReservationStateMachine` and `InventoryUnitStateMachine` | lines 626 (to `CANCELLED`) and 743 (to `COMMITTED`) for reservations. It also imports the unit machine, but my grep showed no call to it. |
| `src/inventory/catalog.service.ts` | `InventoryUnitStateMachine` | line 755, `currentStatus` to `targetStatus` |
| `src/inventory/defect.service.ts` | `InventoryUnitStateMachine` | line 123, forces the unit to `DEFECTIVE` |

- **Which rules affect which services:**
  - Changing `InventoryUnitStateMachine` affects `inventory.service.ts`, `catalog.service.ts` and `defect.service.ts`.
  - Changing `ReservationStateMachine` affects `reservation.service.ts`.
  - `CanonicalOrderStateMachine` and `OrderStateMachine` have no callers in `src/inventory`.
  - `inventory.service.ts` and `catalog.service.ts` import `InvalidStateTransitionError`, but I didn't find them using it beyond the import.
- **Error handling:** `src/server/api-v2.ts:2491` matches on `err.name === "InvalidStateTransitionError"` and returns HTTP 409. A rule change that makes a previously allowed transition throw will surface there as a 409.
- **Tests:**
  - `src/domain/domain.test.ts` covers the Reservation and Order machines (the Order tests use the deprecated `OrderStateMachine`).
  - `src/inventory/catalog-submission.test.ts` asserts `InventoryUnitStateMachine` throws on an invalid transition (line 327).
  - `src/inventory/reservation.test.ts` and `vault.test.ts` matched my first search on "transition" but not on the class names, so I haven't confirmed they depend on the machines.
- **Limits:** I only searched `.ts` files under `src`. I didn't check `app/`, `test/` or other directories. The `test/` folder has several inventory-related tests that matched "transition", and the DB migrations may enforce similar status rules in SQL. I didn't read the transition tables themselves.
